text: The cap a per-owner queue count is measured against is queue.capacity_cap when the queue sets one, and queue_member.capacity otherwise; the 150 of the legacy criteria is a queue cap, not a personal one.
why: The legacy story fixes one cap per queue and the target model carries both a queue cap and a personal capacity, so the answer needs one rule to be testable and two readers must not compute atCap differently.
read: Section 8 BR6, section 11 and section 12.1 of the app story, and AC3 of the contract story, as the cap in force per queue.
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2011-APP section 8 BR6, section 11 and section 12.1; RWB-P3-E2011-CON AC3, section 11 and section 12.7.
confirm: Product owner for queue and caseload rules, at the baseline review of RWB-P3-E2011-CON.
impact: If the personal capacity governs, atCap flips for every member whose capacity differs from the queue cap, and the seed data of TC-E2-011-02 needs one member at the other capacity so the two rules can be told apart.

text: The team queue summary is computed live from recovery_case and the open SERVICE_LEVEL timer of each case, and the reconciled queue_measure snapshot is read only as a reconciliation check; the five answer fields are openCaseCount and breachCount integers, oldestAgeDays integer, oldestEntryDate a date, and owners[] with an integer openCaseCount and a boolean atCap.
why: The legacy screen must equal the case list count at the moment it is read, which a snapshot published on a schedule cannot guarantee, and the target table names different measures than the legacy answer, so one of the two must be declared the source.
read: Section 11, section 12.1 and section 13 of the app story, and AC3 and section 11 of the contract story, as the source and the types of the queue summary fields.
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2011-APP section 11, section 12.1 and section 13; RWB-P3-E2011-CON AC3, section 11 and section 12.7.
confirm: Solution architect with the owner of the queue-measure story of RWB-SVC-P3, at the baseline review.
impact: If the snapshot is declared the source instead, the count and the oldest age can lag the case list by one refresh and TC-E2-011-11 must read the snapshot time as well as the count.

text: rwb-case reads the business date from GET /api/recovery/source-data/v1/data-products/freshness, caches the answer for the request and the business date, sets X-Data-As-Of on the two case answers, omits the header when the answer does not arrive inside the 2 s budget, and the composite route fills the {product} of MSG-P1-001 with the data product name the screen shows.
why: The freshness fact belongs to rwb-source-data in the target and the case service no longer reads the ACE batch record, so the header and the banner need one declared source and one owner of the placeholder.
read: Section 4 step 4, section 12.1, section 12.2 and section 14 of the app story, and AC8 and section 12.2 of the contract story, as the freshness source, the header rule and the placeholder.
applied_in: RWB-P3-E2011-APP section 4, section 12.1, section 12.2 and section 14; RWB-P3-E2011-CON AC5, AC6, AC8 and section 12.2.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-source-data owner, at the baseline review of RWB-P3-E2011-CON.
impact: If the path or the placeholder owner changes, only the freshness client and the banner wording change; no count, no order and no right in either story changes.
